Content:
Let's consider the number [MATH: -1.] We can plot it on a number line, as follows:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f9c9f1a2ed9f2c20547990ff1da72d1f]

Content:
All of the numbers to the left of [MATH: -1] are less than [MATH: -1.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/38f0396b9a48d1f902385b54b9c4665f]

Content:
On the other hand, any number to the right of [MATH: -1] is greater than [MATH: -1.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3b6c91cb7f9cb0e0a459fb8a4092232a]

Content:
The same idea is true for all numbers. For any given number:

Content:
- all numbers to the left on a number line are smaller
- all numbers to the right on a number line are larger

items.title: Comparing Two Points on a Number Line

sections.normalized_html:
Which of the following is true regarding numbers [MATH: A] and [MATH: B?]

  1. [MATH: A < 0]

  2. [MATH: 0 > B]

  3. [MATH: B < A]
sections.readable_text:
Which of the following is true regarding numbers [MATH: A] and [MATH: B?]

[IMG: /graphics/696e9ed336e5580cb8c3176feb05402f]

1. [MATH: A < 0]
2. [MATH: 0 > B]
3. [MATH: B < A]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is true. The number [MATH: A] is to the left of zero. Therefore, [MATH: A] is smaller than [MATH: 0,] which we write as [MATH: A < 0.]

  • Statement II is true. The number [MATH: B] is to the left of zero. Therefore, [MATH: B] is smaller than [MATH: 0,] which we write as [MATH: B < 0.] This is the same as saying that [MATH: 0] is greater than [MATH: B,] which we write as [MATH: 0 > B.]

  • Statement III is false. The number [MATH: A] is to the left of [MATH: A.] Therefore, [MATH: A] is smaller than [MATH: B,] which we write as [MATH: A < B.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
